Operation contracts
-------------------

An operation contract declares a native operation's facts once. A theory of
a module declares one vocabulary and its operations as equations:

  cesta operations check MODULE THEORY
  cesta operations rows MODULE THEORY
  cesta operations metta MODULE THEORY
  cesta operations tables MODULE THEORY
  cesta operations protocols MODULE THEORY
  cesta operations header MODULE THEORY -o OUTPUT.h

check reads the table, refuses malformed declarations with a reason, and
prints the normalized form. rows prints the lists and rows a runtime keeps,
derived from the table; header prints the same as ordinary C X-macros, and
metta as (query-head SPELLING EFFECT) lines for a runtime's execution-contract
specification.

Declaration
-----------

  (Vocabulary) == (Vocabulary "cesta-operation/1"
    (Resources (Resource space "store") (Resource work "scratch") ...)
    (Charges transition ...)
    (Profiles he_extended prime ...))

  (work_take) == (Operation "cesta-operation/1"
    (Spelling "work-take") (Symbol work_take) (Dispatch "special")
    (Forms (Form (Arg EVALUATION DEMAND OWNERSHIP) ...) ...)
    (Footprint (Reads RESOURCE ...) (Writes RESOURCE ...))
    (Context (Blocks YES-NO) (Branches YES-NO) (Progress P) (Charges C ...))
    (Result R)
    (Declared (Static YES-NO) (TypePure YES-NO) (Speculative YES-NO)
              (Replay "transparent"|"refused" [(Through ARITY ...)]))
    (Profiles P ...))

Resources   each is a "store", which a query observes, or "scratch".
Spelling    the operation's name as programs write it.
Symbol      a C identifier for its rows; quoted when the module language
            keeps the word as a keyword, (Symbol "let").
Dispatch    "grounded" (a value operation on closed values), "control",
            "special" or "unknown".
Forms       one form per accepted arity; each argument's evaluation ("value",
            "atom"), demand ("data", "whnf", "source-type", "shape", "value",
            "structure", "pattern") and ownership ("borrow", "consume").
Footprint   what the operation's head reads and writes, never its operands';
            the runtime composes operands. (Footprint "unknown") when no one
            has established it.
Context     blocking, branching, progress ("single", "bounded", "steps",
            "suspends") and the cost charges it makes.
Result      "fresh", "shared" or "borrowed".
Declared    the columns a runtime keeps for its own reasons: static dispatch,
            the type-level conversion licence, admission under speculation,
            and replay, with the arities a replay scan passes through.

Any word may be "unknown" where it says so above, and (Forms) or (Profiles)
may be empty: a fact no one has established is never read as a default. In
particular an unknown footprint is not an empty one.

Checks
------

A table is refused when a name, spelling or symbol repeats; a resource,
charge or profile is undeclared; two forms share an arity; a replay passes
through a form the operation lacks; a word is not one of the admitted words;
a type-level operation declares a read or a write, branches or blocks; a pure
grounded operation lacks the type-level licence; or an operation that writes
is admitted under speculation.

Derived rows
------------

  Static        the operations declared static.
  Pure          grounded operations whose footprint is known to be empty.
  TypePure      type-level operations beyond Pure.
  Speculative   operations admitted under speculation beyond Pure.
  Query         known footprints that touch a store: 2 if the operation writes
                one, else 1 if it reads one.
  Unknown       operations whose footprint is unknown.

Evidence
--------

MeTTapedia's OperationContracts proves, for footprints: the Boolean
independence check is the resource frontier's Independent (a write consumes
and produces its resource); two footprints are independent exactly when the
two operations' access rights (none, read, consume) are separate at every
resource; an operation that reads and writes nothing is independent of every
operation. Under an explicit Conforms hypothesis (each concrete footprint lies
within its declared one), operations with independent declared footprints have
the same causal dependency view in either order. Two operations with
independent footprints can still be told apart by an ordered-stream observer,
so ordered output needs a certificate of its own.

For tables: tableOk is the decidable check above; admitted_laws states what
it guarantees of every operation; the derived rows are lowerRows, and a
recorded query row carries an operation's derived effect, while operations
the runtime admits under speculation are not known writers. The admission
decides that the printed table keeps its laws and that the printed rows are
its derived rows. Large tables are decided in chunks joined by proved append
lemmas, comparing names through an injective code into the natural numbers.

Not proved: that a C handler stays within its declared footprint. That is the
Conforms hypothesis, tested where it is tested, never claimed.

Shared tables and cost protocols
--------------------------------

tables prints the shared cesta-tables/1 representation of operation
identities, resources, charges, profiles and their reference relations.
Their uniqueness and reference checks use the same validator as registry
and counter data. Effect laws still use OperationContracts.

A vocabulary may additionally declare, after Profiles:

  (ChargeKinds (step analysisStep) (transition quantum) (other "unknown"))

Each label must be declared in Charges, appear at most once, and name a
NativeCostLedger.Kind or explicitly remain unknown. An omitted association
is unknown. An operation may add (ProgressBound N): N is positive, and only
bounded progress or single progress with N=1 permits it. Single progress
defaults to bound 1; other omitted bounds are unknown.

protocols prints one cesta-operation-protocol/1 record per operation, with
exactly its charge labels in declaration order, their associated native
ledger kinds, its progress and inspection bound, and replay permission.
The existing check and rows formats are unchanged. The protocol record
does not itself claim a concrete handler's termination or invoice accuracy.

OperationCostProtocol uses the existing NativeCostLedger event valuation
and Cursor protocol. It proves exact retained-budget accounting, chronological
invoices including paid failure/suspension, inert terminal states, budget
and inspection-call bounds, composition across scheduler pauses, and fresh
replay billing. Unknown charge kinds are refused rather than charged zero.
A decreasing rank on an actual handler continuation proves finite cursor
observation; a written bound alone does not. Zero billed work alone cannot
guarantee termination. Controls cover all these distinctions.

Admission checks operation labels, progress, replay and bound well-formedness.
The legacy normalized operation record omits the vocabulary's kind mapping
and an optional numeric bound, so that check alone cannot establish those
two source associations. test-operation-protocol separately compares the
actual normalized profiles with independently specified fixture mappings
and bounds, and rejects their corruption. Neither check establishes a C
handler's effects, invoices or progress refinement; those remain explicit
implementation obligations.
